descriptionChirho: An adjective describing one who has been deprived of children or young, whether through death, miscarriage, or barrenness. All 6 occurrences carry the same core meaning of loss of offspring, applied to both humans and animals (e.g., a bereaved bear in 2 Sam 17:8, Hos 13:8). The split between masculine/feminine and conjunctive forms is purely grammatical inflection, not semantic distinction. Multilingual evidence confirms a single sense: eng 'bereaved / and bereaved,' spa 'sin hijos / y privada de cría,' hin शोकित / और बाँझ, arb مُثكَلٍ / وِ شَكُلَّه, kor 자녀 잃은 / 그리고 잃은 자, swa waliofiwa na watoto / na aliyeharibika.
